BUSADDRE declares AD_ZIP CHAR 9, plus address-type and email fields. Address-role codes must be confirmed before excluding agent/person addresses. ZIP5 and ZIP4 must remain separate in normalized outputs; no postal deliverability or physical-site proof is established.

Monthly creation and weekly subscription do not establish full-versus-delta delivery, delete/correction handling, checksums or replay. The layout has no reviewed version/date or compatibility promise.

Publisher designation confirms the sales channel, not downstream retention, transformation, geocoding or redistribution rights. Those remain contract questions.

candidate.price: Active Business Data costs $30 once or $30 each week. Full bulk offers a request path for eligible noncommercial users and a separate commercial request/license process; this project has not claimed eligibility.

observed_evidence: The current full Business Bulk Data guide has moved to a new media URL and publishes stronger identity/address contracts. These do not remove the separate Active Business Data product's unresolved lifecycle and controlling-license gates.
Active Business Data provides names and primary addresses once or weekly. Full Business Bulk Data is a distinct active/inactive product with master, history and name/address records.
No supported unattended MBLS bulk download API was established; guides describe portal delivery.

Active guide publishes 16 columns with File Number plus Business Filing Type as composite key; filing dates may be partial and primary party names may be individuals. Full bulk separately guarantees static non-recycled Master ID across record types, publishes party/address domains and separate postal extension. Its schema must not be attributed to Active Business Data.

Active output reflects filing status when generated, not proof of operation. A disappeared Active row cannot be treated as a documented closure event. Foreign nonprofits lack annual-renewal dates under the Active guide.

The landing page and Active guide differ on Housing Cooperative inclusion. Full bulk includes name reservations and trademarks, which require separate classification; neither product is a census of operating sites.

Active output provides ZIP and extension separately and identifies a primary business address without a full published value domain. Full bulk separately distinguishes principal, registered-office, mailing, home and agent address roles; geocoding must preserve those distinctions.

Active filenames identify run date; full bulk has export dates, monthly creation and complete related-record sets for supplied businesses. Neither establishes a verified Active deletion/replay/checksum contract or current control totals.

Account/order prerequisites remain. Full bulk guide describes monthly creation and Transaction History delivery within ten days; it does not authorize portal automation. Active weekly ordering does not establish unattended extraction rights.

The full-bulk license allows customer access in normal business but restricts substantial bulk resale/repackaging and sublicensing, and excludes updates absent a separate agreement. Which license governs Active Business Data remains unresolved; the full-bulk grant cannot be transferred by inference.
